newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN SHARES EDGE DOWN AS INVESTORS CATCH BREATH.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN SHARES EDGE DOWN AS INVESTORS CATCH BREATH.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were mixed in early morning trade on Monday, with many stocks easing from record high levels as investors regrouped after last week's market rally, traders said.
Dealers saw buying and selling interest but differed on where the market would end the day.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 569.06, a hair off Friday's record 569.23 close.

Rossiisky Kredit Bank's head of trading and securities Oleg Martynenko saw prices fluctuating throughout the trading session as investors restructured portfolios in the wake of gains from record high closes last week.

"There was a strong rise and now is the perfect time to restructure portfolios," he said. "There is fighting going on between bids and asks right now and it is difficult to say who will win by end of day."

National power company UES slipped to $0.4465 at 0855 GMT from $0.4575 on Friday, and international long-distance provider Rostelekom eased to $4.88 from $5.05. Local utility Mosenergo ticked down to $1.68 from $1.70.

Renaissance Capital trader Viktor Pitaleff saw bargain hunting by Western and Russian investors keeping levels steady over the day, although players would keep a wary eye on Wall Street, which lost 156.78 points on Friday to end at 8031.22.
"We're seeing some bottom fishing and the interest is there -- just enough to keep the market up," he said.
"Everyone will be anticipating the opening of New York -- if everything goes well there then the market should stay about the same."
